title: Seller quickfire: 30s vignettes for integration teams
body:
Purpose:
A pocket-ready set of 30-second vignettes and 1-minute followups tailored to integration engineers, platform architects, and security owners. Use these as voice lines in discovery, quick demos, or to hand off to an SE during a pilot kickoff. The goal is to convey credible engineering tradeoffs (latency, cost, reliability) and a recommended next-step that brings the conversation toward a pilot or technical spike.

How to use:
- Pick persona vignette based on the attendee list; open with the 30s one-liner, then deliver the 1-min backstop if they probe.
- Keep metrics concrete (SLOs, token/unit economics, throughput) and offer a short follow-up action: triage ticket, pilot card, or canary checklist.

Persona vignettes (30s one-liner + 1-min backup):
1) Integration Architect — "Predictable throughput with reserved pools: no noisy neighbors, consistent p95 latency."
   1-min backup: "We offer Dedicated capacity you reserve by the hour/day. Typical customers see p95 tail latencies drop by ~30–50% versus bursty shared routes because of isolated GPU pools and pinned batching parameters. We can sketch an autoscale policy in 30 minutes and run a 2-week throughput soak to prove numbers you care about."
   Quick metric: "Target p95: < 120 ms for prompt sizes up to 1k tokens on select model variants."
   Close ask: "Can we add an evaluation run with your 50th-percentile request trace? We’ll simulate it on Dedicated and share a short report."

2) Platform Engineer — "Keep the same API across hosted and private deployments so your CI and rollouts don't change."
   1-min backup: "Redwood exposes a single API and rollout abstraction that maps to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. That means your feature flags, A/B canary rules and tracing hooks work identically across environments — less ops friction during migration."

3) Security / Compliance Lead — "Bring inference into your VPC with KMS and audit logs; no data leaves your network unless you want it to."
   1-min backup: "Private deployments give you a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and configurable audit retention. For regulated use cases we also support an air-gapped on-prem bundle. If governance is the blocker, let’s schedule a 30-min security deep-dive with our compliance engineer."

4) Product Manager (cost-focused) — "Cut per-token cost by workload-aware caching and model routing while preserving quality."
   1-min backup: "We automatically suggest prefix/KV caching and routing to quantized model variants for non-critical queries. Typical customers see 15–40% cost reduction on retrieval-heavy workloads with no noticeable quality regression on measured prompts."

5) SRE / Reliability Owner — "Automatic fallbacks keep user-facing features live if a top-tier model is unavailable."
   1-min backup: "We let you define fallback chains by policy (latency-first, cost-first, or quality-first). For each route you can configure golden prompt tests; during rollouts we run canaries and revert automatically on regressions."

6) Buyer / Procurement (exec shorthand) — "Reserve capacity for predictable spend and get pricing that supports production SLAs."
   1-min backup: "Reserved Dedicated contracts convert usage volatility into predictable run-rate with options for burst credits. We can build a two-line pricing illustration based on your 30-day token projection."

7) Edge / On-prem Architect — "Deploy the same inference stack behind your firewall with optional air-gapped install."
   1-min backup: "Our Private product supports VPC and on-prem variants; we provide a customer-managed control plane and an ops playbook for upgrades and hotspot mitigation. For latency-sensitive edge inference we recommend smaller warm-up KV caches and pinned model slices."

8) Observability / Developer Productivity Lead — "Token-level cost and traceable latencies for every route so teams can optimize without guesswork."
   1-min backup: "Console shows token breakdowns, per-route SLOs, error causes, and a trace that links application request->model response. Suggest an ops dashboard demo and a short trial with synthetic traces."

9) ML Engineer (quality focused) — "Pin model versions and run quality evals against your prompt set before any rollout."
   1-min backup: "We support model versioning, canary evaluation harnesses, and regression alerts tied to prompt suites. For new model onboarding we recommend a seeded eval set and a 72-hour canary with automated rollback on metric drift."

10) CTO shorthand — "Unified inference, cheaper token economics, and fewer late-night outages."
   1-min backup: "We centralize serving runtime, routing, and rollout abstractions so engineering teams don't build custom stacks. That lowers run-time cost and reduces incident surface with built-in fallbacks."

Quick rebut lines for common objections (10–20s each):
- "Latency will be unpredictable on shared nodes": "We can show a side-by-side p95 report from your sample trace mapped to Dedicated vs Hosted within 48 hours."
- "We store sensitive data": "Private deployment with customer KMS and configurable audit retention — we’ll schedule security onboarding and an SOC2 artifacts package."
- "We can’t change app logic for fallbacks": "Fallbacks are policy-driven and can be configured at the API gateway level so app code needn’t change."
- "Pricing is unclear for high-throughput": "We’ll model your 30-day token mix and return a micro-scenario showing unit cost with and without batching/caching enabled."

Micro-deck (leave-behind 3 slides):
1) Slide 1: TL;DR + one-line value prop for their persona (include expected p95 / unit cost lies).
2) Slide 2: Quick architecture sketch mapping their infra to Redwood (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + one recommended pilot approach.
3) Slide 3: Next steps and pilot acceptance criteria (data to share, success metrics, who to involve).

Pilot/POC checklist (minimal):
- Share 1–2 days of request traces (anonymized) or representative prompt set.
- Define target SLOs (latency p95, throughput) and cost targets.
- Decide deployment type: Hosted quickproof / Dedicated reserved pool / Private pilot.
- Agree on telemetry: token logs, error traces, and a weekly sync.

Rapid diagnostics cheat-sheet (for SEs during call):
- Ask: "What's your 95th/99th percentile latency today and token mix?"
- If latency > 300ms: push Dedicated or smaller prompt shapes + KV caching.
- If cost is primary: propose quantized variants + routing cold paths to cheaper models.
- If security is primary: propose Private + KMS + audit export path.

A/B quick experiments to propose post-call:
- Experiment A: Route 30% of non-critical traffic to quantized-8bit variant for 1 week; measure qualitative drift and cost delta.
- Experiment B: Enable prefix caching on chat sessions > 3 messages; measure tokens saved/week.

Example script for SE handoff (Slack snippet):
"Thanks for the call — per our discussion, we'll run a 72-hour throughput soak on Dedicated with your anonymized trace (ETA: Thurs). SEs: @Ethan to set up the canary run; @Rosa to request KMS questionnaire if they choose Private. Acceptance: p95 < 150ms OR cost per 1k tokens <= $X. Please confirm."

Testing and measurement definitions to agree early:
- p95 latency: measured at our edge before tokenization.
- Unit cost: fully-loaded server cost / generated tokens (include reserved amortization if Dedicated).
- Quality regression: measured by their seeded eval set (f1 / BLEU / human pass-rate depending on task).

Risks & mitigations (one-liners):
- Risk: Unexpected quality drift on quantized models. Mitigation: short AB + human-in-loop checks, automatic rollback.
- Risk: Network egress/data residency. Mitigation: Private deploy + VPC peering / air-gapped option.
- Risk: Ops ownership disputes. Mitigation: clear runbook + SLOs in contract + early runbook dry-run.

Next steps (recommended per-call):
- Immediate: Request a 48–72h sample-run (traces or prompts) and pick deployment type.
- Short (1 week): Run one AB experiment (quantized routing or caching) and deliver a short report with p95 and cost delta.
- Medium (2–4 weeks): Pilot on Dedicated or Private with agreed SLOs and rollback criteria.

Open questions to capture during discovery:
- Average prompt length and common token mixes?
- Peak QPS and expected baseline throughput for first 90 days?
- Is there an internal procurement timeline for reserved capacity?
- Which security certifications / reports do you need pre-pilot?

Notes to seller: keep these vignettes conversational, avoid heavy infra diagrams on the first call, and always land with a concrete next-step (trace upload, pilot kickoff, or 15-min security review).

Document provenance: created by Maya Chen (SE enablement lead). Iteration plan: collect feedback from field team over next 2 weeks and publish v0.2 with 6 new persona soundbites and two sample micro-decks.
